brief: Now that the cursor advertises the click, the handler's last branch is caught making its promise in the wrong place. SIDE and ROAD are the paving of the WHOLE town — the lane, the cross street, the plaza, the quay, the towpath — and every one of them answers 'You scatter crumbs onto the lane', then spawns birds clamped into LN_WALK_N..LN_WALK_S, which lands them down in the lane however far east you clicked. Give the eastern paving its own answers and its own birds: the plaza around the fountain, the quay with the water right there, the cross street, the towpath on the far bank. One place, one line, and birds that land where you actually pointed. The bug is pre-existing; the pointer cursor from #13 is what turned it into a broken promise.
successLooksLike: A click on the quay says something about the quay and the birds land on the quay; likewise the plaza, the cross street and the towpath. No click anywhere in town mentions the lane unless you clicked the lane.
avoid: Do not add a seventh KIND of response — the six that exist are good, and this is about the one that fires in five places while knowing only one of them. Keep the existing bird cap and the daylight>0.2 gate. LAW: one predicate, one definition — decide which place a cell is in exactly once.
